claims.claim: Co-op sessions suffer from disconnects and severe input delay caused by network code architecture.

citations.review_text:
Halo 1 was a good retro experience.

Halo 2 was okay until the Quarantine Zone mission. I was doing co-op and it just doesn't work reliably. The game kept disconnecting. We tried the mission after that one but it also disconnected halfway through the level. Unplayable.

I'd love to recommend this, but the co-op netcode is truly atrocious and I cannot fathom why it functions the way it does.

In most games, at least these days, when you connect to a server, you control your character on your pc, and it sends updates to the server for other players to see. In MCC, you control the server entity *directly* - meaning you have to wait for the server update for your inputs to work.

I have 300ms ping to my friend in the US - in many games, this is slightly rough but bearable. In this game, I press a movement key and have to *wait 300ms for my character to start moving*. I start shooting and *have to wait 300ms for the gun to fire*. Playing a game like that is absolutely impossible, and I'm baffled it works like this:(

I was really looking forward to playing this game with my friend, but this made that completely impossible. How on earth this is still an issue after 7 years (or more counting Xbox release) is beyond me.

claims.claim: The collection includes a graphics toggle feature that lets players switch between original and remastered graphics in real time by pressing the Tab key.

citations.review_text: A fantastic collection of campaigns and multiplayer. I would start here if you are a new Halo fan instead of Campaign Evolved. The ability to toggle between new and old graphics at the press of a button is a great idea and is well implemented. Plenty of legacy options to choose from as well like having a lowered crosshair is also a welcome addition.

The things I like about Halo1:

So far Halo 1 is fun, you can press TAB to switch from the new graphics to the old one.


The things I don't like about Halo1:

I was having trouble with the stage I'm at in Halo1, so I just wanted to reload my save point to restart instead of dying so I pressed "Restart" and the game restarted the whole level because I pressed "Restart".

The only other option was "Last checkpoint" which is not what I want either lol 

I don't like the way vehicules are driven. I get it, it was on Xbox and you needed a system that is fool proof, well it's not. It's the most anoying thing ever.

This is the definitive way to play Halo. Halo Master Chief collection offers nearly every single Halo experience from Reach all the way to Halo 4, allowing you to play through multiple campaigns, multiplayers etc. The insane amount of achievements spread across all campaigns and multiplayers leaves plenty to go for. Multiple difficulties for every campaign allows you to challenge yourself depending on what your looking for.

The Halo Campaign Evolved anniversary edition even allows you to switch between the original graphics settings and the new remastered settings on the fly by simply pressing TAB. It's awesome

Overall if you are even remotely a fan of halo, or are looking for a way to jump in and enjoy the story in order then there is no better way than this collection. If you ever find it on sale, its a instant buy. 

Thanks for reading.

If you grew up playing Halo, this collection is a perfect throwback that feels just right. If you didn't, it's still one of the best ways to experience one of gaming's most influential first-person shooter series.

Six games, lots of exciting missions you'll remember, amazing music, and multiplayer that still works really well today. The option to switch between original and enhanced graphics in Halo: Combat Evolved and Halo 2 isn't just a fun feature—it's an interesting way to see how much game development has advanced over time. The campaigns are still the best part, with great scenes to remember, good co-op play, and a game that still feels fun to play even after many years.

That said, the collection isn't perfect. The PC release had some problems at first, but things are much better now.However, you might still come across some glitches, issues with matching players, or a UI that doesn't work consistently. Some games had more improvements than others, which made the whole experience feel a bit inconsistent.

It's still tough to complain when you're getting six legendary games all in one package. No matter if you're here for the campaigns, Forge, Firefight, or multiplayer, there's way too much content for the price.

Pros:

Six amazing Halo games all in one collection.
* Timeless campaigns with co-op support
Great value for the amount of content.
* Classic/remastered graphics toggle is brilliant
* Active enough multiplayer to enjoy

Cons:

* Occasional bugs and matchmaking issues
* UI can be clunky
Some titles are easier to keep in good condition than others.

Even though it has some issues, Halo: The Master Chief Collection is a tribute to one of the biggest and best gaming series ever. It's not perfect, but if you like playing first-person shooter games, it's definitely worth having.

Recommended.

claims.claim: Reviewers report hit registration issues, specifically identifying Halo and Halo 2 as the worst offenders in multiplayer.

citations.review_text: I suppose after 1100hrs and the better part of playing Halo for nearly 25 years, I should leave a review for Halo MCC. The core game is as close to the original as I'll probably see in my lifetime. I love it and will play it until my dying day. My only gripe, aside from obvious stuff like the matchmaking lobby, is the hit registration.  Halo and Halo 2 are the worst offenders here. I refuse to play Halo 1 MP because it's that bad. Halo 2 is pretty close. Overall you're crazy not to own this. When all the other FPS are doing slides, sprint, wall climbs etc,, Halo makes you take the damage like the terrible player that you are. Lastly, England and their teabags are what makes life worth living. If you love making tea, you'll love Halo MCC.

[h1] It's a good way to Play Halo [/h1]

MCC is for all of us that played the Original Bungie games from Halo Combat Evolved on the OG Xbox since 2001 all the way till Halo Reach in 2010 all of Bungies game still hold up... and then there's Halo 4.
There are many problems with MCC with some of the original Game engines not running like they did on launch day, Unbalanced Matches when doing PvP, Co-op Disconnections during games with friends or PvP, and many more that I am not aware of.

Unless you have an ORIGINAL XBOX from 2001 or a 360 to play the old Halo games this is unfortunately this will do, thankful it's not awful.

I am glad to still be able to play my childhood games and do these games with friends.

claims.claim: Reviewers describe the collection as offering high value, bundling multiple campaigns and multiplayer content for a low price.

citations.review_text:
if you are new to the games, you are going to love them and you WILL be impressed with how much you get for the value. 
If you're like me and have been playing for 25 years, you will love the ability to marathon these games and do cross-game playlists. 
Oh and the multiplayer is still lit. 
It's Halo. This is like owning the Mona Lisa for $39.99

[h1] 10/10 - Amazing Franchise [/h1]

Halo has been very near and dear to me for over a decade, although I have 173 hours at the time of this review I have thousands on Xbox and on each of the originals. And from my experience with MCC I cannot stress how much I implore anyone reading this and considering Halo to get it. For a cheper price than entire triple A games today with common sales you can get 6 whole games with multiplayers and extra modes involved as well as moding capabilities from the workshop.

[h3] Story - 7.5/10 [/h3]
The story is quite good for an FPS game, it is no Telltale game levels of good or detailed but you will get attached to characters and be hooked to the plot with well written stories in each entry. Behind the hood is a lot of lore to get stuck into if you want with overall a very good story to guide you along.

[h3] Graphics - 7.5/10 [/h3]
The graphics of Halo is quite timeless in my opinion, however it would be foolish to say it wasn't getting a bit dated over 25 years. However, even in the oldest of them you can find beauty in the environments with great atmosphere and attention to detail despite the age of these games. From the dreamy snowy areas from Halo CE to the Jungles of Halo 3 or rainy night city in Halo 3 ODST, these game seriously hold up with visuals and atmosphere and graphics isn't much of a concern. This game is quite easy to run for most people due to the age of the games and you will mostly have no trouble playing at good frames (Halo 2 Anniversary is a ♥♥♥♥♥ to run on some levels). I do have to add, do not play Halo CE on the anniversary graphics, it fails to uphold what the original devs intended and is widely considered an absolute sin to play that way next to killing marines.

[h3] Music - 9/10 [/h3]
Nothing much to say here, the music made is iconic and extremely good with many people not even having played the game knowing some of them. It adds heavily to atmosphere or the level and are straight up absolute banger…

An absolute masterpiece of a collection and quite frankly, one of the greatest value propositions in all of PC gaming. This is the ultimate gaming time capsule in my opinon.

It’s no secret that the collection had a incredibly rough borderline shocking launch years ago. But the developers stuck with it and after years of meticulous updates and PC optimization with feature additions, the Master Chief Collection stands today as a flawless triumph ngl. You are getting six legendary games (usually at a quite frank steal when on sale), fully remastered with cross-play, Forge, and a unified multiplayer ecosystem for less than the price of a single modern AAA title.

Here is how the legendary saga breaks down:

>>>The Games<<<
HALO: COMBAT EVOLVED ANNIVERSARY: The blueprint that changed the industry forever. The sense of isolation on the mysterious ring world, the brilliant enemy AI and that iconic orchestral score still hit just as hard today. The ability to swap between the classic graphics and the remastered visuals with a single button press is a brilliant touch even if the classic atmosphere remains unmatched.

HALO 2: ANNIVERSARY: This is the gold standard of what a remaster should be in my opinion; the rewritten cutscenes by Blur Studio are breathtakingly beautiful looking like a modern sci-fi film. Mechanically it introduces dual-wielding and splits the narrative between the Master Chief and the Arbiter, expanding the lore of the Covenant in a deeply engaging way.

HALO 3: The grand finale of the original trilogy and a masterclass in sandbox design. Every level feels like an epic sweeping battlefield. The gunplay, the vehicles and the environmental storytelling culminate in one of the most satisfying conclusions to a gaming trilogy ever conceived.

claims.claim: Reviewers note that the collection lacks split-screen support.

citations.review_text: Love all these games. However not having splitscreen still after all this time is a major let down.

Played through the whole thing solo on Legendary to get myself ready for the next Halo. That's a lot of hours with a controller in my hands, and most of them were good ones. The campaigns still hold up. Legendary solo is still Legendary solo. No complaints about the games themselves.

My problem is with what this collection is supposed to be. It's called the Master Chief Collection, and the pitch has always been "every Halo in one place." Except it isn't. Halo 5 isn't here. Infinite isn't here. Halo Wars isn't here. I get that there are technical and licensing reasons, but I'd have paid for DLC to fold them in without thinking twice. Having to bounce between three storefronts and two launchers to play a series that ships as a single package is exactly the problem this collection was made to solve.

Then there's the unlocks. There used to be cosmetics you earned by finishing every campaign on Legendary — a genuine badge, the kind of thing you'd only have if you'd actually put in the work. They patched that. Now you can just buy them. I found this out after the fact, which somehow made it worse. If the reward for the hardest thing in the game is also sitting in a storefront, the achievement stops meaning anything. It doesn't break the game, but it takes the air out of a playthrough I specifically undertook to earn something.

So: the games are great, the collection is fine, and the stewardship is disappointing. Buy it on sale, play the campaigns, don't expect the definitive Halo package the name promises.
